definitions.meaning: a clumsy bricklayer could literally let one of his bricks fall
to say something tactless or socially embarrassing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a tactless blunder, and a careless builder could also literally let one fall.

clue.text: Most of song in Russian sounded the same at the end

definitions.text: sounded the same at the end

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: Red was a common term for a Soviet Russian

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a hymn is a religious song

explanation.surface: Most of a song in Russian had matching sounds at the ends of lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the song's last letter; 'Red' for Russian is a Cold War convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that share their final sounds are said to chime this way, as lines of verse do.

clue.text: Chinamen have pointed joints, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: knees that are sharp might be called peaky knees

explanation.surface: Men from China are said to have sharp knees.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pekinese are people of Peking (Beijing), so men from China.

indicators.note: something cracked is broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Many a bell has surely cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of saying yes, of course.

clue.text: In picture, one American actress swallows a drink

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the actress's name takes the drink inside it

parts.note: Mae West was an American actress
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star is photographed downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to see it in the mind's eye.

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: Vegetables hauled on board a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A keel is a flat-bottomed boat or barge, especially on the Tyne.

definitions.meaning: a flatfish of the plaice family
to thrash about helplessly, as in a bog

explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish, and a verb meaning to stagger or thrash about with difficulty.

indicators.note: to be heard signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: stationary means still, not moving

explanation.surface: Papers that are still waiting to be listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing materials such as paper and envelopes.

indicators.note: something led astray goes off course, so the letters of the clue word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A papal envoy is lured off the straight path by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Gosh! Retired ruler enters state sports competition

indicators.note: one group of letters goes into another, as a person enters a building

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the exclamation is written backwards

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise like gosh!
a khan is a ruler in central Asia

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise as a former ruler turns up at a state sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' applies to the exclamation, not the ruler; 'enters' puts both inside the abbreviation for Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is an equestrian sporting event, a meeting where riders compete in contests.

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for the colour gold
to dust is to clean by wiping

explanation.surface: Something valuable, or else a cleaning job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a mere link between alternatives, but in heraldry OR means gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare and much sought after is said to be like gold dust.

clue.text: Puts on, so to speak, what's: made for taking off

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word for the clue phrase is spoken rather than written

parts.note: to put on extra is to add, so puts on means adds

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up, as it were, in clothes designed to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts on' suggests dressing, and 'taking off' undressing; the tool takes off shavings of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodworker's tool has an arched blade used to shave and trim timber.

clue.text: Plead a map's used wrong projection

indicators.note: letters used wrongly are put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea that a map's projection was misused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' suggests map-making but is the lump at the front of the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bump of cartilage at the front of a man's throat sticks out.

parts.note: monte is a card game (three-card monte)
to video is to record on tape

explanation.surface: An excellent game to film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Uruguay.

definitions.meaning: the title by which a governor is addressed, as in Your ...

explanation.definitionFit: A title of honour for a governor or ambassador, and an old word for outstanding quality.

definitions.meaning: a store for weapons and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is an arms store, and Arsenal is a north London football club.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: to span something is to cover it from side to side
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone hides a stolen painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal photograph.

clue.text: Manifestation of vengeance makes curse go haywire

indicators.note: something gone haywire is out of control and disordered, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Divine wrath turns a curse wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip or affliction sent as punishment.

clue.text: Shelter provided by doctor in city to lady

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A doctor in town gives a woman a place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that protects from rain, and more generally a cover or shield.

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Refreshments for railway workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral is a fizzy soft drink in British usage.

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it
a till is a shop's cash drawer

explanation.surface: Bears raid the cash register and someone shouts to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt in movement or progress.
A corpse is slang a stiff, and an organised association of people is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Dress left after sailors performed outside

indicators.note: after means the letter for left comes at the end
the verb's letters go round the sailors' abbreviation

parts.note: did means carried out or performed
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A dress abandoned once sailors had done their show outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirndl is an Alpine peasant dress with a full skirt.

clue.text: Lawmen hold one, pound back-that may be

indicators.note: one word holds the others inside it, as a container holds its contents

parts.note: a posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Sheriff's men grab someone and beat him back, which could happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only the pound abbreviation; 'hold' puts the numeral and it inside the lawmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something possible is something that could happen or could be true.

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 21 across in its sense of a group of people

explanation.definitionFit: A company of people acting together, and a group of musicians.

parts.note: to career is to rush or run headlong
along means together with others, as in come along with us

explanation.surface: Pursue a career working within a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a job but is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Run along is a dismissive way of telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Relax and get three points at, end of game

indicators.note: the compass letters are placed after the card game, at its end

parts.note: loo is an old card game
S, E and N are three points of the compass

explanation.surface: Unwind after scoring three points at the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three points' suggests a football win, but these are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken or ease a grip makes it less tight.

clue.text: Something super to play with — my old man told me not to

definitions.text: my old man told me not to

parts.note: a dilly is slang for something excellent or remarkable
to dally with is to trifle or play with

explanation.surface: Something great to toy with, which father forbade.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is from the British music-hall song 'My old man said follow the van, and don't dilly-dally on the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's father warns against loitering or dawdling on the way.
